key_insight: PolyBO speeds up expensive Bayesian optimization by generating higher-quality pseudo-experimental data with an adaptively updated polynomial regression model.
engineering_relevance: It is especially useful for long-running scientific experiments and materials optimization where each trial is costly and the number of real evaluations is limited.
method: Use a low-capacity polynomial regression model to generate pseudo-experimental data.
Adaptively update the model as new experimental results arrive.
Combine real and pseudo-data to train the BO surrogate and propose the next experiment.
evidence_signal: On synthetic benchmarks, PolyBO reduced optimization time by a median of 42%, and on a real materials composition problem it reduced time by a median of 96% versus conventional methods.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the polynomial model approximates the true response surface when only a few real experiments are available.
paper_title: Optimization of time-consuming experimental conditions using pseudo-experimental data guided by adaptive polynomial regression
